criteria.summary: Forty scenarios connect exact run/scenario/input/source/build/content/rules identity to the existing trusted SessionContext epoch and a safe disposable owner alias. The command ordering pair remains separate from trusted owner epoch; malformed pairs are null and retain scenario/attempt identity. Committed events follow counter/revision mutation, while rejections preserve before/after state.

Same-input retries retain one opaque action ID and one unique effect. Fresh runs reset counters and use fresh run-scoped action IDs. Import/startup/missing reports produce no completed action evidence. The deliberate assertion failure retains actual commits only and cannot fabricate the overstated expected count.

All diagnostic run reports and nested raw logs pass sentinel scanning, including private unknown field names, successful secret-bearing inputs and malformed secret-bearing startup input. Only explicitly allowlisted provenance, bounded reason codes and mutation facts are encoded; no raw commands, configuration, private result, actual character ID or arbitrary exception text is copied. At most eight safe findings are emitted while retaining the total finding count. Broader regression projection output with intentionally visible identities is summarized separately in boundary-regression.json.

Canonical Id/Version/CommandContext/ability_command_v2 encodings remain unchanged. Valid omitted optional character IDs, nullable intent fields, zero/max-lossless sequences and rejected missing/null/negative/overprecision ordering are exercised. Four constructed projections use the existing projector for hidden-source recipient scoping, revoked entitlement and hidden-target denial; no probe owner/action identities enter public output.

review.scope: Only test fixtures/runners, local diagnostic encoder, checker integration, regressions and launch documentation changed. Production admission, combat, economy, transport and standards are untouched.
review.ownership: The context probe remains the only mutable counter/revision owner; its optional encoder receives that same trusted SessionContext and only serializes facts after processing. Command parsing and public projection reuse their existing owners.
review.readability: The local encoder owns field allowlisting, the runner owns fixture execution and the Python module owns evidence checks. Longer validation functions were reviewed as cohesive validation of one bounded JSON boundary; no general logging framework or canonical envelope was added.
review.godot: Typed script APIs and bounded collections; native editor import and isolated runner import/check/runtime executed without unexpected errors or warnings. New script UIDs were generated by the pinned editor.
review.security: Caller metadata is constructed by the isolated trusted runner. No gameplay RPC or exported production dependency on tests was added. Private finding paths/messages and credential-bearing input are excluded from diagnostics.
review.lifecycle: Fresh disposable projects, bounded child timeouts and teardown; fresh successful execution after every failure control. Prior evidence is preserved.
not_applicable: Connected server/multiple peer transport test: this ticket uses logical isolated probes and changes no networking.
Gameplay combat/economy/durable persistence execution: explicitly outside ticket scope.
Graphical/browser verification: no visual UI change; generated documentation receives content/link/consistency checks.

limitations: Test-only disposable counter/revision; no live character, economic ledger, combat or durable-success claim.
Public projection samples are constructed inputs, not executed combat.
No wire traffic, connected client, capacity, external database or deployment verification.
